best_parts: node tis_t and tis_ok: names the old FNAC key as 'quick', says why core gives histology and receptors, and a sure_note asks the learner to check what the pathologist must report
node cut and cut_h: the stem asks for a relative factor, the trap is 'a fixed 5 cm rule', and the hint asks whether the factor is fixed or depends on the breast; a clean examiner-grade contrast
node numb_t: separates how dramatic a deficit is from how often it occurs, which is the exact PYQ confusion (winging versus intercostobrachial numbness)
cold section (axil, numb, tam, labc, male) has no hint buttons while the first four probes do, so the unaided check is real, as the playbook asks
flaws: node male_p: 'Early menarche, a long reproductive lifespan' is a female-only risk factor in a question about men, so it is dominated and eliminable at once (DP2)
node labc_p: 'Radiotherapy first to shrink the tumour' is an absurd first step for fixed nodes and loses every pairing with the key (DP2)
node axil: the key is the longest option (68 characters against 63 for the trap); node labc and male keys are also longest, so the key is findable by form (DP1)
node reg: the stem's 'Your registrar says, Every new lump gets a mammogram first' names the trap rule in the stem, so the probe tests recognition of a quoted error rather than the choice
whole segment: no learner-built summary (the blueprint goal) and no recap; the path runs straight to @next after the male probe, and there is no fast lane for experts

best_parts: node p9: three options (BRCA1 trap, BRCA2 key, PTEN partial) with a plausible partial; the feedback separates BRCA1's triple-negative link in women from the male link
node p6: the tamoxifen bleeding vignette with a partial 'switch to an aromatase inhibitor without examining the uterus' that tempts a learner who knows the drug change but not the order of care
node p1: the booking-clerk stem puts the age qualifier in the scenario, with MRI as a plausible partial; each trap and each partial name a distinct wrong model
node p11-style items are absent, but p5 and p8 keep one trap per probe with hint-then-retry on the first half only, a clean cold second half for the report
flaws: node p10_p: 'Simple mastectomy with no axillary surgery' is dominated for an operable cancer and loses every pairing with the MRM key (DP2)
node p7: the stem 'The team says a 6 cm tumour rules out breast conservation on size alone' states the trap as the team's claim, so the key is cued by form (DP1)
node p1_hint: 'which works in a young, dense breast' nearly names ultrasound, so the hint gives away the key rather than the question
whole segment: feedback opens 'It is tempting because...' on nearly every trap, so the voice is formulaic (R8); no learner-built summary and no fast lane; the path ends at @next with no recap

best_parts: node p11: one probe carries two traps (axillary clearance first, bone scan first) with the key 'SLNB and breast surgery, no routine bone scan', so the learner must place the axilla and the staging in one stem; the best cold-check item of the three
node p1: the cytology 'suspicious, cannot exclude malignancy' stem frames the core-versus-FNAC choice as a real clinical decision with a sensible hint
node p6: the nerve probe pairs each nerve with its deficit; the feedback separates how dramatic a deficit is from how often it occurs
flaws: node p1 to p10 (except p5 and p11): the correct reply is the first option in ten of eleven probes, so the key is findable by position (DP1)
nodes p2, p3, p4, p6, p7, p8, p9, p10 are two-option probes (one key, one trap), so the key is a 50/50 guess and the path says little beyond trap versus correct (DP2, R9)
node p9: the stem 'The plan on paper says surgery first' names the trap in the scenario, which gives away the answer
whole segment: 11 probes against the playbook's cap of 8 to 10 new stems; p11 is one node but two traps, and the recap node 'wrap' adds a tell without a learner-built summary

merge_ideas: a's spine (tis, reg, bone, cut, axil, numb, tam, labc, male) with b's three-option male-gene probe (BRCA1 trap, BRCA2 key, PTEN partial) in place of a's two-option male probe
b's tamoxifen probe with the 'switch to an aromatase inhibitor without examining the uterus' partial, replacing a's tam probe, so the cold check tests order of care as well as the drug
c's p11 combined probe (clearance first and bone scan first in one stem) as the penultimate item, so two traps are tested together in the cold half

a's dominated partials (menarche, radiotherapy-first) replaced by b's plausible partials (PET-CT for every early cancer; excision of the whole lump), and key length and position balanced across the nine probes
add a short learner-built summary at the end (choose and order three rules: sample, staging scan, axillary step) as the blueprint goal asks, with a recap line and no more than 10 new stems in total
